author: Code & Coffee Team
content:
Welcome to Code & Coffee Philadelphia! Whether you’re a seasoned developer, a designer, or someone just starting their tech journey, our community has something for everyone.
What We’re All About Code & Coffee Philadelphia is more than just a meetup group – we’re a thriving community of tech enthusiasts who believe in the power of collaboration, learning, and good coffee. Our mission is to create an inclusive space where people can share ideas, work on projects, and grow their skills together.
Types of Events We Host Weekly Meetups Every week, we gather to work on projects, share knowledge, and connect with fellow developers. These casual sessions are perfect for:
Getting help with coding challenges Finding collaborators for your projects Learning new technologies Building your professional network Technical Workshops We regularly host hands-on workshops covering:
AI and Machine Learning - From paper discussions to practical implementations Web Development - Modern frameworks, best practices, and emerging technologies Mobile Development - iOS, Android, and cross-platform solutions DevOps and Cloud - Infrastructure, deployment, and scaling applications Special Events Throughout the year, we organize larger events like:
Hackathons (like our recent Philly Tech Week Innovation Hackathon) Tech talks by industry professionals Project showcases Career development sessions How to Get Involved 1. Join Our Meetup Group The easiest way to stay updated on events is through our Meetup page. You’ll get notifications about upcoming events and can RSVP to secure your spot.
2. Attend an Event Don’t be shy! Our community is welcoming to people of all skill levels. Come as you are, bring your laptop, and be ready to learn and contribute.
3. Contribute to Projects We’re always working on community projects. Check out our:
Tech Talent Matchboard - Connecting local professionals Project Request System - Get help with your coding challenges Event Sponsorship Program - Partner with us to support the community 4. Follow Us Online Stay connected through our social media channels:
LinkedIn: Code & Coffee Philadelphia Instagram: @philly_codes What to Expect at Your First Event Atmosphere Our events are casual and friendly. You’ll find people working on laptops, discussing technical challenges, and sharing knowledge over coffee (or tea, if that’s your preference).
Format Most events are self-directed. You can:
Work on your own projects Join a group working on something interesting Ask for help with coding problems Participate in discussions about technology trends Networking While networking happens naturally, we’re not about forced interactions. Connections form organically through shared interests and collaborative work.
Success Stories Our community has been the launching pad for numerous success stories:
Startup Formations - Several companies have been born from collaborations at our events Career Advancement - Members have found new jobs, changed careers, and advanced in their current roles Skill Development - From beginners to experts, everyone learns something new Open Source Contributions - Many of our projects have become valuable community resources Community Guidelines To ensure everyone feels welcome and comfortable:
Be Respectful - Treat everyone with kindness and consideration Be Inclusive - Welcome people of all backgrounds and experience levels Share Knowledge - Help others learn and grow Give Back - Contribute to the community that supports you Looking Ahead We’re constantly evolving based on what our community needs. Some exciting developments on the horizon include:
Expanded Workshop Series - More deep-dive technical sessions Mentorship Program - Pairing experienced developers with newcomers Corporate Partnerships - More opportunities for internships and jobs Regional Collaboration - Working with other tech communities in the region Ready to Join? The best way to get started is to show up! Check our events calendar and come to the next meetup. Bring your curiosity, your current projects, and an open mind.
Questions? Feel free to reach out through any of our channels or just ask when you attend your first event. We’re here to help you succeed and grow in your tech journey.
Welcome to the Code & Coffee family!
description: Everything you need to know about joining our vibrant tech community in Philadelphia.
title: Getting Started with Code & Coffee Philadelphia

author: Code & Coffee Team
content:
Our Philly Tech Week Innovation Hackathon 2025 was an incredible success! Over three days, developers, designers, and entrepreneurs came together to build innovative solutions and push the boundaries of technology.
Event Highlights The hackathon brought together Philadelphia’s brightest tech minds to collaborate on cutting-edge projects. With tracks focused on AI, generative gaming systems, and startup-oriented solutions, participants had the opportunity to work on truly innovative ideas.
Hackathon Tracks Generative Game System Track Participants created next-generation gaming experiences using AI-powered mechanics:
Dynamic Content Generation - Games that create levels, stories, and challenges in real-time AI-Powered NPCs - Non-player characters with realistic behaviors and dialogue Interactive Storytelling - Adaptive narratives that respond to player choices BYO Idea/Other Track This open track welcomed diverse projects including:
Philly-Focused Applications - Tools and apps specifically designed for Philadelphia residents Data Analysis Tools - Solutions for processing and visualizing local data Automation Solutions - Scripts and systems to streamline repetitive tasks Academic Research Applications - Implementations of cutting-edge research Best Startup Oriented Project Projects with clear business potential and commercialization paths:
Market Viability - Solutions addressing real market needs Scalable Business Models - Ideas with clear paths to revenue and growth Investment Readiness - Projects positioned for potential funding Amazing Projects The quality of submissions exceeded our expectations. Teams built everything from AI-powered city planning tools to revolutionary gaming engines. The creativity and technical skill on display truly represented the best of Philadelphia’s tech community.
Expert Judging Panel Our distinguished panel of judges brought diverse expertise:
Arjun Chakraborty - Principal Applied AI Engineer, Microsoft Jivitesh Poojary - Lead ML Engineer, Comcast Praneetha Kotla - Lead RPA Developer, ERP Smartlabs Tony Siu - Founding Computer Vision Engineer, TryVariant.ai Himanshu Hansaria - Machine Learning Engineer, Five Below Derek Meegan - Data and Analytics Senior Associate, Grant Thornton Ruchi Mangharamani - IT Business System Analyst Sr Advisor Zack Light - Software Development Engineer, High Frequency Trading Raphael Namberd - Blockchain Engineer, Blockspace Surya Rao Rayarao - Lead Software Engineer, SS&C Technologies Prizes and Recognition Winners received both recognition and valuable prizes:
Generative Gaming Track: $1,000 cash prize BYO/Other Track: Dinner at Samba Steakhouse with organizers Best Startup Project: $600 value digital marketing consultation and SEO platform access Community Impact This hackathon demonstrated the power of Philadelphia’s tech community. Beyond the competition, participants:
Formed New Partnerships - Many teams continued working together after the event Learned New Technologies - Exposure to AI tools and modern development practices Built Their Network - Connections made during the hackathon led to job opportunities and collaborations Contributed to Open Source - Several projects were open-sourced for community benefit Key Takeaways For Participants Rapid Prototyping Skills - Learning to build and iterate quickly under time constraints Team Collaboration - Working effectively with diverse skill sets and perspectives Pitch Development - Communicating technical concepts to both technical and business audiences Industry Exposure - Direct interaction with professionals from major tech companies For the Community Talent Showcase - Highlighting the depth of technical talent in Philadelphia Innovation Catalyst - Spurring new ideas and approaches to local challenges Network Building - Strengthening connections within the tech ecosystem Skill Development - Providing hands-on learning opportunities What’s Next The success of this hackathon sets the stage for future events. We’re already planning:
Quarterly Hackathons - Regular opportunities for innovation and collaboration Specialized Workshops - Deep-dive sessions on specific technologies Startup Accelerator - Support program for promising projects Corporate Partnerships - Expanded involvement from Philadelphia’s tech companies Join Our Next Event Interested in participating in future hackathons? Here’s how to stay involved:
Join Our Meetup Group - Get notifications about upcoming events Follow Our Updates - Stay connected through our social media channels Attend Weekly Meetups - Build skills and relationships between major events Volunteer - Help organize and support community events Sponsors and Partners Special thanks to our partners who made this event possible:
Comcast Lift Labs - Provided the venue and technical infrastructure Local Tech Companies - Sponsored prizes and provided expert judges Philly Tech Week - Integration with the city-wide technology celebration Community Volunteers - Organizers and mentors who made everything run smoothly The Philly Tech Week Innovation Hackathon 2025 proved that Philadelphia’s tech community is ready to compete on the national stage. We can’t wait to see what next year brings!
Want to get involved? Join our next meetup and be part of Philadelphia’s growing tech community.

author: Code & Coffee Team
content:
Blog Content Management Guide This guide explains how to create and manage blog posts for the Code & Coffee Philadelphia website using Hugo’s page bundles.
Hugo Page Bundles Hugo supports “page bundles” which allow you to organize content and assets together in folders. This makes it easier to manage blog posts with images and other resources.
Blog Post Structure Each blog post should be in its own folder with an index.md file:
content/blog/ ├── your-post-title/ │ ├── index.md # The blog post content │ ├── hero-image.jpg # Featured image │ ├── diagram.png # Other images used in the post │ └── data.csv # Any other assets └── another-post/ ├── index.md └── cover.jpg Creating a New Blog Post 1. Create the Post Folder mkdir content/blog/your-post-title 2. Create index.md with Front Matter --- title: "Your Post Title" date: 2025-06-23 author: "Your Name" description: "Brief description for SEO and previews" topic: "tutorial" # Required: choose from available topics tags: ["javascript", "beginners", "web-development"] # Optional: specific tags featured: false image: "hero-image.jpg" # Optional: header image filename readingTime: 5 # Optional: estimated reading time in minutes --- Your post content here... <!--more--> More detailed content after the summary break... 3. Required Front Matter Fields title: The post title (appears as the main heading) date: Publication date in YYYY-MM-DD format author: Author name description: Brief summary for previews and SEO topic: Primary topic category (see available topics below) tags: Array of specific tags for detailed categorization 4. Optional Front Matter Fields featured: Set to true to mark as a featured post (shows badge) image: Filename of the header image (place in same folder) readingTime: Estimated reading time in minutes Topics and Tags System Available Topics (choose one) Primary content categories for broad organization:
community - Community updates, member spotlights, general announcements events - Event recaps, upcoming events, meetup information tutorial - Technical tutorials and how-to guides news - Industry news, tech trends, announcements projects - Project showcases, open source contributions career - Career advice, job opportunities, professional development Available Tags (choose multiple) Specific descriptors for detailed categorization:
Technologies javascript, python, react, nodejs, api, web-development ai, machine-learning, data-science, devops, cloud mobile, ios, android, blockchain, gaming Skill Levels beginners, intermediate, advanced Event Types hackathon, workshop, tech-talk, networking, meetup Content Types recap, announcement, showcase, discussion, interview Adding Images Header/Featured Images Place your header image in the same folder as your index.md Reference it in the front matter: image: "your-image.jpg" Hugo will automatically use this for social media previews Images in Content Reference images in the same folder directly:
![Alt text](diagram.png) Or use Hugo shortcodes for more control:
Optional caption
Content Features Summary/Excerpt Add <!--more--> in your content to create a manual summary break. Everything before this tag becomes the excerpt shown in blog lists.
Code Blocks Use fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting:
```javascript function hello() { console.log("Hello, Code & Coffee!"); } ### Links - Internal links: `[Link text](/blog/other-post/)` - External links: `[Link text](https://example.com)` ## Blog Publishing Workflow ### 1. Local Development ```bash # Start Hugo development server hugo server -D # View your post at http://localhost:5000 2. Publishing Create your post folder and index.md Add any images or assets to the same folder Test locally with hugo server Commit and push to trigger automatic deployment 3. Automatic Updates Hugo automatically:
Generates the blog listing page Creates tag pages Updates the RSS feed Builds related posts suggestions Updates the sitemap Example Post Structure content/blog/building-rest-api/ ├── index.md # Main content ├── api-diagram.png # Referenced in content ├── postman-screenshot.jpg # Referenced in content └── cover.jpg # Featured image --- title: "Building Your First REST API" date: 2025-06-23 author: "Alex Johnson" description: "Learn to build REST APIs with Node.js and Express" topic: "tutorial" tags: ["javascript", "nodejs", "api", "beginners", "backend"] featured: true image: "cover.jpg" readingTime: 8 --- Building REST APIs is essential for modern web development... <!--more--> ## Setting Up the Project First, create a new directory... ![API Structure](api-diagram.png) Here's how to test with Postman: ![Postman Testing](postman-screenshot.jpg) Best Practices Use descriptive folder names - lowercase with hyphens Optimize images - compress before adding to reduce load times Write compelling descriptions - these appear in social media previews Choose relevant tags - typically 3-5 tags per post Include reading time - helps readers plan their time Use the summary break - control what appears in post previews Test locally first - always preview before publishing Maintenance Review tags periodically to ensure consistency Update older posts if information becomes outdated Monitor featured posts to keep them current and relevant Check image links if you move or rename files
